name: Shadowthread Cave
summary: Shadowthread Cave lies beneath the northwest cliffs of Shadowglen, where its spiders have grown dangerous. Their brood now threatens young kaldorei near Aldrassil.

sections.title: A Brood Growing Restless
sections.body: Shadowthread Cave opens in Shadowglen’s shaded northwest, a lair for Teldrassil’s giant spiders. In earlier years, the spiders lived quietly alongside the World Tree’s young boughs. Now they guard their territory fiercely. Webwood silk chokes the stone corridors, and the brood threatens young kaldorei venturing beyond Aldrassil.

sections.title: Githyiss the Vile
sections.body: Githyiss the Vile rules the deepest recesses of Shadowthread Cave. The monstrous broodmother is far more ferocious than the common webwood crawlers. Young night elf sentinels and druids go into the cave to curb the infestation and slay Githyiss, keeping the corruption touching Teldrassil’s wildlife from overrunning Shadowglen’s sanctuary.

faq.answer: Shadowthread Cave lies in Shadowglen’s northwest corner, against the rocky hillside bordering Teldrassil’s night elf starting valley.

faq.q: Why are the spiders in the cave so aggressive?
faq.answer: Spiders have always dwelled in Shadowthread Cave, but a foul sickness and growing imbalance across Teldrassil have driven local wildlife mad. The webwood spiders have become exceptionally violent.
Githyiss the Vile is a massive, venomous webwood spider matriarch in the deepest part of Shadowthread Cave. She is the mother of the aggressive brood threatening young kaldorei in Shadowglen.

faq.q: What makes the cave valuable despite the danger?
faq.answer: Dense layers of naturally spun webwood silk fill the cave. The arachnids in its dark chambers weave this valuable, resilient crafting material in great numbers.

angles.text: As a young night elf, you face one of your first trials in defending your sacred home from creeping corruption: clearing Shadowthread Cave and slaying Githyiss the Vile.
As a druid, you can read the Webwood brood’s unchecked aggression as a troubling sign that Teldrassil’s natural harmony is deeply disturbed.
